sample_unit: patients (external validation cohort; 6,347 in MIMIC development cohort)

links.outcome: Performance drop when comparing development population to external cohort, attributed to population heterogeneity
links.effect: Performance decay attributed to significant population heterogeneity (e.g. BMI differences) and specific cardiac surgery pathophysiology not captured by general ICU variables.
links.quote: The performance decay was attributed to significant population heterogeneity (e.g. BMI differences) and the specific pathophysiological milieu of cardiac surgery not fully captured by general ICU variables.

links.outcome: Model discrimination on external local cohort versus internal test set
links.effect: PR-AUC fell from 0.888 (MIMIC internal) to 0.309 in the external AHXY cohort; AUC fell from 0.709 to 0.548, near-random.
links.quote: However, upon deployment in the external AHXY cohort, the model exhibited significant performance attenuation, with the PR-AUC dropping to 0.309 and the AUC decreasing to 0.548.

links.outcome: Model unsuited to local population without adaptation
links.effect: Near-random predictive performance externally (AUC 0.548), indicating lack of generalizability without further adaptation; recalibration or transfer learning recommended.
links.quote: This near-random predictive performance indicates a lack of direct real-world generalizability without further adaptation.

links.outcome: Generalization of ICU-trained model to a specialized cardiac surgery population
links.effect: General ICU model showed substantial cross-domain transferability gap; AUC 0.548 and PR-AUC 0.309 in cardiac surgery cohort.
links.quote: General-purpose ICU models may face a substantial cross-domain transferability gap without local adaptation when applied to specialized sub-specialties like cardiac surgery across different demographic populations.

screen.reason: The study develops an AKI prediction model on MIMIC and conducts external retrospective validation on an independent cohort, finding significant performance drop. It evaluates generalizability and transferability across centers but does not test a specific deployment safeguard/practice (such as testing recalibration directly).
